plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the disk method for computing the volume of a solid of revolution. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing region R bounded above by the curve y = f(x), below by the x-axis, and between x = a and x = b; a rotation arrow at x = b indicates revolution about the x-axis. Panel (b): a 3D perspective of the resulting solid; at a generic position x along the axis, a circular disk cross-section is highlighted in blue with radius f(x) labeled, showing that each cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a disk of area pi[f(x)]^2. The figure derives the disk method formula V = integral from a to b of pi[f(x)]^2 dx by identifying the cross-sectional area at each x and integrating along the axis of revolution.

elements: x-axis: horizontal arrow pointing right, labeled 'x'
y-axis: vertical arrow pointing up, labeled 'y'
Panel (a): curve y = f(x) drawn in blue from x=a to x=b, rising and slightly concave near b, labeled 'y = f(x)' above the curve
Panel (a): shaded light-blue region R between the curve and the x-axis over [a,b], with vertical left edge at x=a and vertical right edge at x=b
Panel (a): label 'R' centered inside the shaded region
Panel (a): tick marks and labels 'a' and 'b' on the x-axis
Panel (a): small circular rotation arrow wrapping the x-axis near x=b indicating revolution about the x-axis
Panel (b): 3D solid of revolution generated by rotating R about the x-axis, drawn with black silhouette outline (upper and lower profile curves)
Panel (b): left end cap ellipse at x=a drawn as a thin gray ellipse (radius f(a))
Panel (b): right end cap ellipse at x=b drawn as a bold black ellipse (radius f(b))
Panel (b): highlighted blue circular disk cross-section at a generic x, drawn as a filled light-blue ellipse with a bold blue rim
Panel (b): red dot marking the point (x, 0, 0) on the axis at the disk center
Panel (b): vertical radius segment from the axis point up to the top of the disk
Panel (b): curly brace beside the radius segment with label 'f(x)'
Panel (b): x-axis line running through the solid, with tick labels 'a', 'x', 'b'
Panel captions '(a)' and '(b)' below each panel
Readout of radius f(x) and disk area π[f(x)]², and the volume integral V = ∫ₐᵇ π[f(x)]² dx

interactions.teaches: each vertical segment of height f(x) in R traces a full circle of radius f(x), so the cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a disk

interactions.teaches: the disk radius at each x is exactly f(x), so the formula alone determines the entire profile of the solid and the limits fix how much of it is built
interactions.label: Region definition

demo_steps.title: The region R
demo_steps.narration: In the xy-plane, R is bounded above by y = f(x), below by the x-axis, and on the sides by x = a and x = b. The circular arrow at b marks the axis of revolution.

demo_steps.title: Revolve about the x-axis
demo_steps.narration: Spinning R a full turn about the x-axis sweeps out a solid. Every vertical segment of R becomes a circle.

demo_steps.title: One disk cross-section
demo_steps.narration: Cut the solid with a plane perpendicular to the x-axis at x. The slice is a disk whose radius is exactly f(x), so its area is π[f(x)]².

demo_steps.title: Slide the cut toward b
demo_steps.narration: As x moves toward b the radius f(x) grows and the disk area π[f(x)]² grows with the square of it.

demo_steps.title: Change the curve
demo_steps.narration: Edit f(x) or the limits and the profile, the disk, and the volume all update together: V = ∫ₐᵇ π[f(x)]² dx.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units = graph units. x-axis spans -1 to 6.5 (arrow at right), y-axis spans -2 to 3 (arrow at top); origin at screen-left of the figure with a and b to its right. Default f(x)=sqrt(x) scaled so f(b)=f(5)≈2.24; a=0.5, b=5. Panel (a): curve drawn in medium blue #29ABE2 (line width ~3px), region R filled light blue #BFE2F2 with thin blue vertical edges at x=a and x=b; label 'R' at about (2.7, 0.7); label 'y = f(x)' at about (2.2, 2.0) above the curve; small rotation ellipse-arrow centered on the x-axis just right of b, drawn in black. Panel (b): the solid is the surface of revolution of the SAME f about the x-axis, axis horizontal running screen-left to screen-right; silhouette outline black #000 at ~2px, surface rendered light gray/white (#F5F5F5, MeshStandard, double-sided, slight transparency 0.15 so the interior disk is visible). Left cap ellipse at x=a in thin gray #AAAAAA, right cap ellipse at x=b in bold black. The highlighted disk sits at the current slider x (default 2.2, left-of-center in the source): filled #BFE2F2 at ~0.75 opacity with a bold #29ABE2 rim ~3px, oriented in the y-z plane (normal along +X). Red dot #E8443A radius ~0.07 at (x,0,0). Radius segment black from (x,0,0) up to (x,f(x),0); curly brace just to the right of that segment with 'f(x)' label. Tick labels a, x, b sit below the axis. Camera slightly above and to the right of the axis so circles project as ellipses with about a 1:3.5 minor:major ratio, matching the source. Axes and labels use black; axis arrows are small filled cones.
interactionPlan.notes: Build panel (a) as flat geometry in the z=0 plane (ShapeGeometry for R, Line/TubeGeometry for the curve) and panel (b) as a LatheGeometry-like mesh built from sampled f(x): construct a BufferGeometry by revolving the sampled profile points about the +X axis (parametric ring sweep, ~120 radial × ~160 axial segments), recomputing vertices whenever the equation_input or bounds change. Silhouette outline: draw the upper and lower profile curves as fat lines in the camera-facing plane, plus EllipseCurve rims at x=a, x=b, and x=slider. Use math parser (e.g. a small expression evaluator) for f(x) with inline error text if parsing fails; clamp a<b and guard f(x)<0. The revolve animation sweeps a rotation angle 0→2π applied to the profile surface while the flat region stays drawn, then settles into panel (b). Orbit should be limited (azimuth ±40°, elevation −5°..40°) so the figure keeps its textbook reading. Overlay HTML/CSS2D labels for y, x, a, b, x, f(x), R, y = f(x), (a), (b), and a live readout 'f(x) = …, area = π[f(x)]² = …' plus the integral V = ∫ₐᵇ π[f(x)]² dx with a numerically integrated value.

authoredContext:
Let f be continuous and nonnegative on [a, b], and let R be the region that is bounded above by y = f (x), below by the x-axis, and on the sides by the lines x = a and x = b (Figure 5.2.9a). Find the volume of the solid of revolution that is generated by revolving the region R about the x-axis. We can solve this problem by slicing. For this purpose, observe that the cross section
of the solid taken perpendicular to the x-axis at the point x is a circular disk of radius f (x)
(Figure 5.2.9b). The area of this region is
A(x) = π[f (x)]

Because the cross sections are disk shaped, the application of this formula is called the
method of disks

discrepancies: No text labels appear at all in the rendered output — the source's y, x, a, b, x, f(x), y = f(x), R and the (a)/(b) panel captions are all absent on screen, leaving the figure unannotated.

Panels (a) and (b) are drawn simultaneously and overlaid: the flat blue region R sits inside the translucent grey solid together with the highlighted disk, whereas the source separates them into two distinct panels (the code's updateVisibility/mode switching evidently never takes effect).

Camera framing is wrong: the figure is not framed to the content (tiny object in a large empty canvas, oblique 3/4 view) instead of the source's front-on axis view for (a) and near-side view for (b); the code calls a non-scaffolded `setCameraView(...)` rather than `setStandardView(...)`, so the intended poses never apply.

Interactive controls (panel A/B buttons, revolve, f(x)/a/b inputs, x slider, Prev/Next demo) appear inert — the guided-demo title/text and the numeric readout panel are blank in the render, indicating the event listeners and label creation after the camera call never executed.

Source-figure annotation details are not legible/visible in the render: the circular rotation arrow near b (present in the code but essentially invisible at this scale), the brace marking f(x), and the tick marks at a, x, b.
The solid's silhouette reads as a smooth flaring cone rather than the source's characteristic profile with a thin grey rim at a and a heavy black rim at b clearly distinguished.
evaluation.notes: The code contains a well-conceived disk-method figure (region R, revolve animation, disk cross-section, integral readout), but the render shows it failing to initialize past the camera call: no labels, blank demo/readout text, both panels drawn on top of each other, and an unframed oblique view, so the delivered artifact is neither recognizable nor interactive.
action_items: Replace the non-existent `setCameraView({projection,...})` call with the scaffolded `setStandardView({azimuth, polar, heightFraction})` (and guard `document.getElementById('btnReset')` with a null check) so the rest of the script — labels, demo steps, and all event listeners — actually runs.

Ensure `updateVisibility()` runs on init so only panel (a) (region R, curve, rotation arrow, a/b ticks) shows by default and the solid/disk/silhouette appear only in panel (b) or during revolve; never render both overlaid.
Frame the camera to the content (heightFraction so the solid fills ~70% of the canvas) and use a front-on view for (a) and a slightly-above near-side view for (b) matching the source.

Restore and enlarge the annotation set — italic y, x axis labels, a, b, x tick labels, the f(x) brace label, 'y = f(x)', 'R', and the (a)/(b) caption — with a clear size hierarchy (caption/R larger than axis letters).

demo_steps.narration: Cut the solid with a plane perpendicular to the x-axis at x. The slice is a disk whose radius is exactly f(x), so its area is π[f(x)]².

demo_steps.title: Slide the cut toward b
demo_steps.narration: As x moves toward b the radius f(x) grows and the disk area π[f(x)]² grows with the square of it.

demo_steps.title: Change the curve
demo_steps.narration: Edit f(x) or the limits and the profile, the disk, and the volume all update together: V = ∫ₐᵇ π[f(x)]² dx.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units = graph units. x-axis spans -1 to 6.5 (arrow at right), y-axis spans -2 to 3 (arrow at top); origin at screen-left of the figure with a and b to its right. Default f(x)=sqrt(x) scaled so f(b)=f(5)≈2.24; a=0.5, b=5. Panel (a): curve drawn in medium blue #29ABE2 (line width ~3px), region R filled light blue #BFE2F2 with thin blue vertical edges at x=a and x=b; label 'R' at about (2.7, 0.7); label 'y = f(x)' at about (2.2, 2.0) above the curve; small rotation ellipse-arrow centered on the x-axis just right of b, drawn in black. Panel (b): the solid is the surface of revolution of the SAME f about the x-axis, axis horizontal running screen-left to screen-right; silhouette outline black #000 at ~2px, surface rendered light gray/white (#F5F5F5, MeshStandard, double-sided, slight transparency 0.15 so the interior disk is visible). Left cap ellipse at x=a in thin gray #AAAAAA, right cap ellipse at x=b in bold black. The highlighted disk sits at the current slider x (default 2.2, left-of-center in the source): filled #BFE2F2 at ~0.75 opacity with a bold #29ABE2 rim ~3px, oriented in the y-z plane (normal along +X). Red dot #E8443A radius ~0.07 at (x,0,0). Radius segment black from (x,0,0) up to (x,f(x),0); curly brace just to the right of that segment with 'f(x)' label. Tick labels a, x, b sit below the axis. Camera slightly above and to the right of the axis so circles project as ellipses with about a 1:3.5 minor:major ratio, matching the source. Axes and labels use black; axis arrows are small filled cones.
interactionPlan.notes: Build panel (a) as flat geometry in the z=0 plane (ShapeGeometry for R, Line/TubeGeometry for the curve) and panel (b) as a LatheGeometry-like mesh built from sampled f(x): construct a BufferGeometry by revolving the sampled profile points about the +X axis (parametric ring sweep, ~120 radial × ~160 axial segments), recomputing vertices whenever the equation_input or bounds change. Silhouette outline: draw the upper and lower profile curves as fat lines in the camera-facing plane, plus EllipseCurve rims at x=a, x=b, and x=slider. Use math parser (e.g. a small expression evaluator) for f(x) with inline error text if parsing fails; clamp a<b and guard f(x)<0. The revolve animation sweeps a rotation angle 0→2π applied to the profile surface while the flat region stays drawn, then settles into panel (b). Orbit should be limited (azimuth ±40°, elevation −5°..40°) so the figure keeps its textbook reading. Overlay HTML/CSS2D labels for y, x, a, b, x, f(x), R, y = f(x), (a), (b), and a live readout 'f(x) = …, area = π[f(x)]² = …' plus the integral V = ∫ₐᵇ π[f(x)]² dx with a numerically integrated value.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the disk method for computing the volume of a solid of revolution. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing region R bounded above by the curve y = f(x), below by the x-axis, and between x = a and x = b; a rotation arrow at x = b indicates revolution about the x-axis. Panel (b): a 3D perspective of the resulting solid; at a generic position x along the axis, a circular disk cross-section is highlighted in blue with radius f(x) labeled, showing that each cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a disk of area pi[f(x)]^2. The figure derives the disk method formula V = integral from a to b of pi[f(x)]^2 dx by identifying the cross-sectional area at each x and integrating along the axis of revolution.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- equation_input for f(x) and the interval: one field pre-filled with "sqrt(x)" and two fields for bounds a and b; learner edits the function or bounds and the 2D region R redraws, the disk cross-section updates, and the 3D solid of revolution reshapes — teaches that the disk radius at each x equals f(x), so the solid's profile is determined entirely by the formula
- slider for x in [a, b]: sweep the disk cross-section and display radius f(x) and disk area π[f(x)]² at the current position
plan.sourcePath: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.9

discrepancies: Source shows panels (a) and (b) side by side for direct comparison; the generated figure only ever shows one at a time behind a toggle, so the visual pairing of region → solid is lost at a glance (mitigated by the revolve animation).

The source profile rises gently and then flares sharply upward near b (giving the trumpet/bell shaped solid with a large end cap); the default sqrt(x) is concave-down and produces a much blunter, less trumpet-like silhouette than the printed figure.

In panel (a) the source draws the curve meeting the vertical edge at b at its maximum with a distinctly steep terminal slope; the generated version's right edge and top corner geometry is flatter, and the shaded region occupies a smaller fraction of the frame than in the source (large empty area at right).

Panel (b) in the source is a line-art outline (white solid with black silhouette and gray/black ellipse caps); the generated solid is a translucent shaded surface, so the crisp outline look of the textbook is only partially reproduced.
evaluation.notes: A well-constructed and conceptually correct disk-method figure with a rich, genuinely pedagogical interaction set (panel toggle, revolve animation, f/a/b editing, cross-section slider, guided steps); main shortfalls are the single-panel-at-a-time presentation and a default curve/proportion that does not reproduce the source's flared trumpet profile.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items were flagged, verification passed, and all scores are solid with only minor stylistic/default-curve differences remaining.
